newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine president orders new privatisation rules.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine president orders new privatisation rules.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma gave the government and the State Property Fund (FDM) a week to devise a process to privatise enterprises considered strategic to national security, Kuchma's press service said on Friday.
A statement also said the government and FDM, the state privatisation agency, must submit within two weeks a law on privatising companies with strategic foreign investment.
"The goal of the president's directive is to put into order the sale of stakes in companies which have remained in government hands," the statement said.

A government decision last year to privatise more than 200 companies through strategic foreign investment hit a snag last December when parliament halted the privatisations until the government passed a law governing the process.
The government has also started privatising some companies considered "strategic" to national security, although 3,500 are still banned from privatisation under a moratorium placed by parliament.

Ukraine, which has been criticised by international funding bodies for the slow pace of its privatisation programme, plans this year to privatise 1,440 medium and large enterprises and 3,400 small companies.
According to the FDM nearly 10,000 companies are in the process of being privatised.
